newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks surge 2.55pct, construction leads.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks surge 2.55pct, construction leads.

text.p: Construction and investment shares led the Athens bourse rally on Monday with the index climbing 2.55 percent on very heavy volume after the market pierced the 1,300 resistance level on Friday.

"After breaking 1,300 points, the market jumped to new highs. The new resistance level is now set at 1,400 points. During the session we saw a new high at 1,376.76 points," said John Haveles, an analyst at Delphi Mutual Fund.
The Greek bourse is becoming more and more attractive, compared to alternative investment venues, he said.
"Successive good news of easing inflation and interest rates have driven the index up. More and more banks are lowering their deposit rates," he said.

Greece will cut its two-year zero coupon bond rate by 20 basis points to 10.10 percent on February 28. It will also cut 12-month, six-month and three-month T-bills by 40 basis points to 10.5, 9.7 and 9.4 percent effective February 24.
The investment public will continue to focus on inflation which is expected to ease to 6.5 percent in February from 6.8 percent in January, he said.
It is possible that if February inflation does not turn out to be 6.5 percent as predicted but only slightly higher, the market could be adversely affected, he said.
Large construction and cement companies also saw a rise on Monday and will go on rallying as big projects are expected to take off in 1997, he said.
The Athens general share index settled 2.55 percent or 33.99 points higher at 1366.92 points from Friday's 1332.93, after opening at 1339.61. The session's high was at 1376.66 points.
Turnover rose to 34.2 billion drachmas on volume of 9.0 million shares, with many block trades. Advancers led decliners 220 to 28 with 12 issues unchanged.
Construction led the rally with a strong rise of 7.95 percent, while investment shares also rose 7.16 percent.
Construction shares had also led the advance on Friday, warming to strong expectations that Athens will be among the candidates to host the 2004 Olympic Games.
The International Olympic Committee (IOC) gave a favourable review to Athens' bid to host the games. It will shortlist five cities in early March and announce its final decision in September.
"The market has discounted Athens' candidacy. Construction shares seem attractive in light of this event," said broker Giuseppe Giano at Euroxx Securities. Small caps gained 4.27 percent.
